answer: Stake-weighted sortition. Select agents to assess umber pigment, pearl quality, or jetty damage by drawing uniformly from stake units locked before an unpredictable seed appears. The verifier counts each unit once and keeps it locked through the selection window. Splitting one balance across N accounts preserves its total chance of selection; gaining more chances requires more immobilized capital and its opportunity cost. This assumes rewards have no per-account minimum and the seed cannot be biased; either loophole can make identity splitting profitable.
